prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: مواقيت الصلاة في مدن سعودية (language ar, right-to-left: column 1 is on the RIGHT).
Grid: 6 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "المدينة" · longest unbreakable word 49px · one-line width 91px
  col 2: header "الفجر" · longest unbreakable word 35px · one-line width 35px
  col 3: header "الظهر" · longest unbreakable word 35px · one-line width 35px
  col 4: header "العصر" · longest unbreakable word 38px · one-line width 38px
  col 5: header "المغرب" · longest unbreakable word 47px · one-line width 47px
  col 6: header "العشاء" · longest unbreakable word 41px · one-line width 41px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 414px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 413px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"A quick-reference timetable of daily prayer times for six Saudi cities: readers look up one city's day, or compare one prayer across cities.","reading":"Right-to-left: the eye lands on the city name (row header) first, then sweeps left across the five prayer times; the dominant comparison is column-wise (same prayer across cities), with row-wise reading as the secondary mode.","groups":["col 1 (المدينة) is the row identifier and must be visually separated from the data block","cols 2–6 (الفجر، الظهر، العصر، المغرب، العشاء) are five instances of the same kind of value — clock times — and should read as one uniform band, with no column appearing more important than another"],"keep_intact":["every time value, e.g. 8:16, 12:24, 3:23 — they must never wrap or break at the colon","the single-word headers الفجر، الظهر، العصر، المغرب، العشاء, which cannot wrap and set each column's minimum width"],"may_wrap":["city names, especially المدينة المنورة (two words) and مكة المكرمة — wrapping them to a second line is harmless because the row height already accommodates two lines"]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r2A: widths [112, 56, 56, 59, 68, 62] · table 414×255px · row heights [36, 36, 36, 36, 36, 36, 36] · column headers wrapped 0/6 · tallest cell 1 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2B: widths [102, 58, 58, 61, 70, 64] · table 414×278px · row heights [36, 36, 36, 60, 36, 36, 36] · column headers wrapped 0/6 · tallest cell 2 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2C: widths [92, 60, 60, 63, 72, 66] · table 414×301px · row heights [36, 36, 60, 60, 36, 36, 36] · column headers wrapped 0/6 · tallest cell 2 lines · mid-word splits 0

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}

log.raw: {"critique":[{"design":"r2A","good":"The only layout where the grid stays perfectly regular: all seven rows are 36px, every header and every time value is on one line, no mid-word breaks, and the city column at 112px is wide enough for المدينة المنورة to sit on a single line. That width also does the job the brief asks of column 1 — at nearly double a prayer column it clearly separates the row identifier from the five-value time band, and because the five prayer columns are narrow and equal-ish in feel, the eye sweeps left across a continuous strip of clock times.","problems":"Everything is flush to its limit: the header المغرب (47px) exactly fills its 47px of content space, العصر (38) exactly fills 38, and المدينة المنورة (91) exactly fills 91. Nothing has a single pixel of slack, so the band looks slightly pinched next to the generous city column, and the layout is brittle — a font-rendering or rounding difference of 1px would push a header or a city name onto a second line.","cause":"col 1 = 112px is precisely the one-line width of the longest city name (91 + 21 padding). That leaves 301px for the five prayer columns, which is exactly the sum of their minimum widths (56+56+59+68+62). There is zero slack anywhere in the table."},{"design":"r2B","good":"Buys real breathing room for the time columns — الفجر/الظهر get 58 instead of 56, المغرب 70 instead of 68 — so values like 11:56 and 12:24 sit comfortably rather than edge to edge, and مكة المكرمة still holds one line.","problems":"One row (المدينة المنورة) collapses to two lines and grows to 60px, producing a single tall row in a stack of 36px rows. It reads as an accident rather than a decision: the vertical rhythm of the table breaks exactly where the eye is scanning down the city list, and the data cells beside it become a large empty box, which visually over-weights that one city.","cause":"col 1 = 102px gives only 81px of text, below the ~85–91px needed by المدينة المنورة, so it wraps.
